newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed, eye on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed, eye on U.S. data.

* Toronto stocks closed mixed on Wednesday, settling back after early euphoria on unexpectedly weak U.S. data. * Eye on more numbers. * 108.7 million shares traded worth C$1.64 billion.
Toronto stocks lost early gains to close mixed on Wednesday as early euphoria over surprisingly low U.S. producer prices for April subsided.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index dipped 1.06 points to 6248.18. Trading totaled 108.7 million shares worth C$1.64 billion.
The index dipped 0.6 percent versus economists' forecasts for a flat month, prompting waning interest rate hike fears.
Investors were wary as Toronto approached its all-time high of 6348.02 points set on March 11, Donnini said.
Investors are eying more U.S. data due out on Thursday, including April's consumer price index.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices slid, led by heavyweight golds, consumer products and base metals. The gainers included oils and utilities.
Advancers outnumbered decliners 526 to 462, while 298 issues closed flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Gandalf Technologies Inc tumbled 1.04 to 2.44 in heavy trading of 2.7 million shares after Tuesday's gain of almost 150 percent.
After the market closed, the computer networking company reported a fourth-quarter loss of US$0.43 a share for the period ended March 31 versus a breakeven year earlier period.
* Dreco Energy Services Ltd jumped 12 to 65 after news it would merge with National-Oilwell Inc.
* Canadian Occidental Petroleum slipped 0.55 to 28 after announcing that Chief Executive David Hentschel would be replaced by Chief Financial Officer Victor Zaleschuk.
